answers.1: Fulton County's 2027 budget, meaning what the county will spend in 2027. A two-person 'Budget Commission' (Commissioner Bob Ellis for the north half of the county and Vice Chair Khadijah Abdur-Rahman for the south half) is writing the draft, due by Nov 15, 2026. Then 'the full Board' decides. I think the Board means the county commissioners plus Chairman Pitts, but the page never gives its full name. The Board must vote by its second regular January meeting, expected Jan 20, 2027, and it could vote earlier. There is also a fight over the process: whether the two-person commission has too much say, and a 5% limit on how much extra money departments can ask for.
answers.2: The page doesn't say. It never mentions property taxes, a tax rate or my tax bill. It gives no dollar amounts at all: not the budget total, not last year's total, and not what the justice offices want. It says the budget affects 'residents and property owners' but not how. It doesn't explain why it can't tell me. The only related fact is that the draft isn't due until Nov 15, 2026, but the page doesn't connect that to taxes. I can't even tell whether this vote sets my tax rate or whether that is decided somewhere else.
answers.3: It's the county's money, but the page never says where that money comes from. It goes to county departments and services, and the page names the jail, the courts and libraries. Six justice offices (sheriff, district attorney, solicitor-general, court clerk, probate judge and public defender) want more money. They point to staff shortages, court delays and jail overcrowding. A 5% limit caps how much extra departments can ask for, but the page doesn't say 5% of what. The Board can add, cut or move money before it votes. There are no dollar figures anywhere. The 'who pays' details on the Options tab stay hidden until you tap.
answers.4: I can speak during public comment at a Board meeting, in person or by Zoom. The meetings are Nov 18, Dec 2 and Dec 16, 2026, at 10 a.m., in the Assembly Hall of the Fulton County Government Center, 141 Pryor Street SW, Atlanta. I have to send a Zoom comment, or a request to speak in person, before the meeting starts at 10 a.m. The page doesn't say where to send it, except to call. Each speaker gets up to 2 minutes, and Fulton people go first. I can call the Clerk's Office at 404-612-8200 to set a speaking date or to ask how to send a written comment. I can also watch the county's Public Notices page for a budget public hearing, but there's no date yet and no web address is given. I can tell my district commissioner and the chairman what to fund or cut, but the page doesn't tell me my district, who my commissioner is or how to reach them. And I can read the draft when it comes out. By when: before the Board votes. The vote must happen by the second regular January meeting, expected Jan 20, 2027, but it could come earlier. So the meetings I'm sure about are Nov 18, Dec 2 and Dec 16.
answers.5: 'Mixed' isn't used anywhere on the page. 'Uncertain' shows up on every argument card, next to 'Supported' and 'Values question', under 'Evidence, by part:'. The page doesn't define it in what I can see. It points to 'How to read these cards', but that is behind a tap. Every card lists the same three words, so I couldn't tell which part of which argument is uncertain. Some card lines, like 'their effect on the draft isn't known yet', make it sound like it means 'not known yet', but the page doesn't say that.
answers.6: For: the commission gives commissioners 'earlier and ongoing input', balanced between north and south, and the full Board still makes the final decision (Resolution 26-0460). Commissioner Ellis also said the commission's meetings are open. Against: critics, including the justice officials and Commissioner Barrett, say two commissioners get too much say. They say departments have to pitch their needs to a two-person panel instead of the whole Board. Critics also say the 5% limit keeps departments' full requests out of the draft.

'Budget Commission' vs. 'Budget Committee' (the Nov 4 agenda item): same group or a different one?
'Clerk to the Commission', 'Clerk's Office' and 'the clerk': which commission, and are these the same office? (They share a phone number.)
'5% limit' / '5% cap': 5% of what? Who set it, and when? And 'extra money' on top of what?

'The jail agreement' (on the justice funding card): never explained.

'Legistar'.

'Authority' (in 'department, agency, elected official or authority').

'Our framing' vs. 'Our analysis' vs. 'Our math': what's the difference?

Home page, other topics: 'PSC' (never spelled out), 'HB 1009', 'PIA Staff', 'GAM testimony', 'Public witness', 'real-time payments' and 'fuel credit'.
seemed_to_favor: Mostly even and careful. It uses no party labels, and both sides get cards with the same layout. If anything, critics of the current process get more room. The 30-second Summary gives critics two lines and supporters one. Four of the 6 argument cards come from the critics: two marked 'Critical', plus the January-vote and more-money cards, both from the same justice officials. Nothing on the page defends the 5% limit. The page does explain that this reflects who was quoted and that no record gives a reason for the limit. One title read like an accusation: 'Two commissioners, seated under rules they sponsored, have too much say', since the card never shows who sponsored the rules. Overall, I didn't feel pushed toward either side.
hardest: Question 2: the page never mentions property taxes, a tax rate or any dollar amount, so I couldn't tell whether this vote touches my tax bill at all, let alone how much or when. Question 5 was next hardest, because 'Uncertain' isn't explained and every card shows the same three labels.
